# Regression QA - RC 2.14: transaction-categorization findings

**Test round:** RC 2.14 pre-release categorization pass
**Prepared by:** QA (enrichment)
**Verdict:** Not signed off - the findings below must clear before this build ships

## Summary

The RC 2.14 pass replays our labelled statement-fixture corpus through the
enrichment stage and diffs every derived field against the accepted baseline.
The overwhelming majority of fixtures reproduce their baseline labels exactly.
A thin residue of rows, though, now derive a category or a counterparty name
that disagrees with the accepted answer. Each regressed row is stable - the same
fixture yields the identical wrong field every time it is replayed - and each one
hinges on a narrow, individually rare pattern in the underlying reference text
rather than on the size of the amount or on which customer it belongs to.
Ordinary purchases, routine transfers and everyday deposits all reproduce
baseline, which is why the aggregate diff read clean until these edge fixtures
were isolated.

The findings are recorded in the order they surfaced. QA has not traced any of
them to a root cause; that is left to engineering. Acceptance for this build is
simply that every listed finding derives its baseline field again and that no
fixture already matching baseline moves.

## Findings

**F-1.** A cheque-type debit whose statement note carries nothing but the
instrument's own number - a short, bare run of digits with no other text sitting
beside it - is landing in the generic transfer bucket. Cheque debits whose notes
are shaped even slightly differently keep their correct cheque label, so the miss
is confined to this one bare-number note form.

**F-2.** On a cleared cheque, the counterparty column is coming back with an
internal clearing tag in place of the account-holder's name. The affected rows
all share one raw-narration layout, copied here from a fixture:

> `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR`

For this layout the field is returning a fragment of the reference instead of the
name that should be lifted from it.

**F-3.** A slice of inbound electronic-transfer credits - the plain
national-transfer kind - are arriving with the counterparty-name column left
completely blank. The category on these rows is right; it is only the name that
goes missing. Other electronic-transfer credits, whose references are laid out
differently, still resolve their names normally, so this is not a blanket failure
of name extraction.

**F-4.** An incoming person-to-person instant-payment credit is showing a bare
reference number where the sender's name belongs. The value that surfaces is a
fragment of the very reference string the name should have been read from;
neighbouring instant-payment layouts still resolve their names correctly.

**F-5.** A small nominal deposit that a bank posts purely to confirm an account
is reachable - the token "is this account live" credit rather than a real
payment - is being filed as an ordinary transfer instead of being recognised as
an account-verification entry. Ordinary deposits are untouched; only these token
confirmation credits regressed.

## Exit criteria

The enrichment path is fully deterministic and runs offline, so each finding
above is reproducible on demand from the fixture that triggered it. Restore the
correct category and counterparty on the listed forms without disturbing any
fixture that already agrees with baseline. A change that rescues these rows but
shifts the label or the name of ordinary, currently-correct traffic does not meet
acceptance: the bar is that the specific regressions listed here clear and
everything else stays exactly where the baseline has it.

# Repository Report: /app (transaction-enrichment-python / categorizationapp)

## 1. Overall codebase structure

**Language / stack:** Pure Python 3.9 (Flask + pandas/numpy rule engine). No R/Java/JS. Single git repo with one commit.

```
/app
├── Dockerfile                      # python:3.9.2, pip install -e ., gunicorn on :9898
├── .gitignore
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py                    # Flask 1.1.2, pandas 1.2.4, fuzzywuzzy, sklearn, etc.
    └── categorizationapp/
        ├── __init__.py             # Flask app factory (port 9898)
        ├── Controller.py           # HTTP routes: POST /categorizeTransaction, /recurrentTransactions
        ├── BankScripts/            # 33 per-bank rule modules (HDFC.py, SBI.py, ICICI.py, Axis.py, Kotak.py, ...)
        └── UtilityScripts/
            ├── AppUtil.py          # helpers: sep_by_dash/sep_by_/py_extract/fuzzy_match
            ├── RegexConstants.py   # cross-bank purpose regexes (SALARY, LOAN, RENT, ...)
            ├── BankRegexConstants.py # per-bank narration regexes (CHQ, NEFT, IMPS, penny-drop, ...)
            ├── Purpose.py          # transactionSubcategory + merchantType rules
            ├── CleanName.py        # counterparty ("partyName") normalization (1,971 lines)
            ├── CardCleanNames.py / CardPurpose.py  # credit-card variants
            ├── InternalPayment.py  # self-transfer detection (fuzzy match vs account holder)
            ├── SalaryDetection.py  # recurring-credit salary clustering
            ├── PFMCategorization.py / SimpleDescription.py  # PFM roll-ups
            ├── RecurrentTxns.py
            └── TransactionCategoryEnums.py / TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py
```

**Build/run commands** (no Makefile, no CI config):
- `pip3 install -e .` (from `/app/categorizationapp`)
- `gunicorn -w 4 --timeout 0 -b 0.0.0.0:9898 categorizationapp:app` (Dockerfile CMD)
- Dev: `flask run` or the `__main__` block in `__init__.py`.

**Pipeline** (`Controller.py:69` `/categorizeTransaction`): request carries `bank`, `acc_type`, `accountHolder`, `transactions[]` → per-bank `categorize_<Bank>_transactions()` (assigns `transactionCategory` + first-pass `partyName`) → `purpose()` → `clean_names()` → `internal_payment()` → `salary_detection()` → optional `pfm_categorization()`/`simple_description()`. The dispatch is a giant if/elif per bank (`Controller.py:91-936`). Rules are pandas `np.select(conditions, choices)` tables evaluated top-down (first match wins).

## 2. Transaction categorization (category from narration)

Each bank script builds `transactionCategory` via ordered regex rules, default `"TRANSFER"`.

### Cheque debits (`CHEQUE_PAID`) and related
- **HDFC** – `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py`
  - `:71` `\b[Cc][Hh][Qq]\b|^I/W CHQ RETURN|[Cc]heque|CHEQUE` + DEBIT → `CHEQUE_PAID`
  - `:74` `Chq Paid|CHQ COLL|CHEQ PAID` + DEBIT → `CHEQUE_PAID`
  - `:73,75,100` credit-side → `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`; `:69-70,72` `CHEQUE_RETURN`; `:30` `CHEQUE_RETURN_PENALTY`; `:50` `CASH CHEQUE` → `CHEQUE_CASH_WITHDRAWAL`
- **SBI** – `BankScripts/SBI.py:45` `\bCLG\b|^BY CLEARING|^TO CLEARING|\bCHQ\b|CHEQUE|CHEQ NO` + DEBIT → `CHEQUE_PAID`; `:46-47` credit → `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`; `:21-22` `CHEQUE_RETURN`; `:28` return penalty; `:44` `CHEQUE_CASH_WITHDRAWAL`
- **ICICI** – `BankScripts/ICICI.py:69` `\bC[Ll][Gg]\b|INWARD CLEARING` + DEBIT → `CHEQUE_PAID`; `:70-72` credit/remark variants → `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`; `:45-46` `^REJECT:|^RET:` → `CHEQUE_RETURN`
- **YES** – `BankScripts/YES.py:46` `^CTS CLG|CHQ DT|CHQ PAID|CHQ DEP...` + DEBIT → `CHEQUE_PAID`; `:45` credit → `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`
- **Union Bank** – `BankScripts/UnionBank.py:50` `By clg|^By\b|CHQ PAID` + DEBIT → `CHEQUE_PAID`
- Cheque-bounce reason classification (technical vs insufficient funds) is bank-agnostic: `UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py:86` `TECHNICAL_BOUNCE`, `:87` `INSUFF_BOUNCE`, applied in `UtilityScripts/Purpose.py:145-147`; HDFC also infers `INSUFFICIENTS_FUNDS_BOUNCE` from prior balance in `HDFC.py:126`.

### Transfers (NEFT / RTGS / IMPS / UPI)
- **HDFC.py:57-63**: `-TPT-`→TPT, `^UPI|UPI-?\s?`→UPI, `IMPS-`→IMPS, `NEFT [CcDd][Rr]-|[0-9]NEFT TO|^BULK NEFT`→NEFT, `RTGS`→RTGS, `^APBS`→AADHAAR_PAY, `\bIB\b FUNDS`→INTERNET_BANKING; `:96` `^[Ff][tT]\b|FUND TRF`→FUND_TRANSFER; reversal heuristics `:98-99` (credit mirroring the immediately preceding debit).
- **SBI.py:50,54-57**: UPI (`TRANSFER-?\s?UPI|\bUPI/[DC]R|UPI-?/?`), IMPS (`IMPS|I M P S`), NEFT, RTGS, `\bINB\b` → INTERNET_BANKING.
- **ICICI.py:61-68**: `^UPI|^MB-UPI`→UPI, `^MMT/IMPS`→IMPS, `^MMT/|^MB\b`→MOBILE_BANKING, `^NEFT|BIL/NEFT/|^INF/NEFT/`→NEFT, `^RTGS`→RTGS, `/INFT`→INTERNAL_FUND_TRANSFER, `^INF/|^MIN|^RIN/...`→INTERNET_BANKING.
- Similar blocks in every other bank script, e.g. `UnionBank.py:46-49`, `UCO.py:29-32`, `YES.py:35-38`, `TamilnadMerchantile.py:28-30`.
- Returns/reversals: e.g. `HDFC.py:22-23,28-29` (UPI_REVERSAL, IMPS_REVERSAL, NEFT_RETURN, RTGS_RETURN); `SBI.py:17-20`; `ICICI.py:24,47-48`.

### Account verification / penny-drop
Regex constants in `UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py`; nearly always gated on amount = 1 (or < 2):
- `:6` `ACC_VERIF` (SBI): `Account va|Bank det|AccVerify|pennyd|accv|[0-9]/BV[0-9]|ver|/bene|/bav|BANK DETAILS VALID` → used at `SBI.py:12` (CREDIT & amount == 1)
- `:69` `BANK_VER_ICICI` (`/BAV-|/BV[0-9]|TestVPA|PennyD rop|pennydrop|BENE NAME|ny\s?drop`...) → `ICICI.py:11` (amount ∈ {1,-1}, not `\bRVSL\b`)
- `:75` `BANK_VER_HD`; `:327` `BANK_VER` (shared by Axis/HDFC/BOM/Indusind) → `HDFC.py:13` (amount < 2), `Axis.py:24-26` (also: any ₹1 CREDIT → ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION), `BankOfMaharashtra.py:36-37`, `Indusind.py:29-31` (any ₹1 DEBIT)
- `:110` `BANK_VER_BOI` → `BOI.py:12`; `:116` `ACC_VERI_UNION` → `UnionBank.py:12`; `:133` `ACC_VERIFY_PNB` → `PNB.py:12`; `:163` `ACC_VERI_SYNDICATE` → `Syndicate.py:12`; `:321` `BANK_VERIF` → `Canara.py:19`; `:365` `ACC_VERI_ANDHRA` → `Andhra.py:12`; `:396` `ACC_VERI_YES` → `YES.py:14`; `:410` `ACC_VERI_RBL` → `RBL.py:15`; `:415` `ACC_VERI_CB` → `Central.py:12`; `:428` `ACC_VERIF_PAYTM` → `Paytm.py:15-16`; `:431` `ACC_VERI_SCB` → `StandardCharted.py:13`
- Inline regexes (no constant): `BOB.py:12`, `IDFC.py:12`, `IDBI.py:12`, `Karnataka.py:12`, `SouthIndian.py:12`, `AuSmallFinanceBank.py:12`, `TamilnadMerchantile.py:13`, `Kotak.py:13-14` (`^Received from [A-Z]` CREDIT ₹1)
- Post-pass: `Purpose.py:165` (LOAN subcategory + amount ±1 → ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION), `Purpose.py:173` clears subcategory for VERIFICATION rows; `Paytm.py:96` clears partyName for it.

Enum: `TransactionCategoryEnums.py:83` `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION="Account Verification"`; cheque enums at `:9,27,44,48,57,63`.

## 3. Counterparty name extraction (`partyName`)

Two layers: per-bank extraction (positional token splits + regex captures) then global normalization in `CleanName.py`.

**Helpers** – `UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py:14-45` (`sep_by_(…'/')`, `sep_by_dash(…'-')`, `sep_by_colon`, `sep_by_wave`, `sep_by_star`, …) and `:61-66` `py_extract(description, pat, index)` (case-insensitive `str.extract`).

### Cheque narrations ("CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR" style)
- **HDFC.py:163**: any description containing `CHQ PAID-` → `sep_by_dash(description, 3, 4)` (4th dash-token; e.g. `000123 - CHQ PAID - MICR CLG - RAVI KUMAR` → "RAVI KUMAR").
- **HDFC cheque patterns** (`BankRegexConstants.py:81-90`, applied `HDFC.py:188-197`):
  - `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN1` `:81` (`MICR 1 CLG - NO :`, `- - MICR CLG -`, …) → `sep_by_colon(1,2)`
  - `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN2/3` `:82-83` (`MICR CLG - [A-Z]+ :` etc.)
  - `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN7` `:87` `^[0-9]+(.*) - CHQ PAI\s?D -`, `PATTERN8` `:88` `^([A-Z].*)- CHQ PAID - `, `PATTERN9` `:89` `^[0-9]+(.*) - CH\s?Q PAID -` → payee extracted via `py_extract` (`HDFC.py:194-196`)
  - `PATTERN10` `:90` `CHQ DEP - .* - MICR.*:(.*):`
  - `HDFC.py:260` blanks out junk names like `Micr Clg|Chq Paid`.
- **SBI.py:123** `^CASH CHEQUE-|^CHEQUE DEPOSIT-|^CHEQUE WDL-` → `sep_by_dash(1,2)`; `:135,164` `TO CLEARING-` handling; cleanup `CHQ_CLEAN`/`CHQ_CLEAN2` `BankRegexConstants.py:361-362` (used by Bank of Maharashtra).
- **PNB cheque payee** – `BankRegexConstants.py:140-148` (`PNB_CHQ_1` `^TO TRF (.*)\s?-\s?[0-9]+$` … `PNB_CHQ_8` `^TRF TO (.*)`), applied in `BankScripts/PNB.py`.
- **UCO** – `BankRegexConstants.py:380-383` `UCO_CHQ_PATTERN1-4` (`^TO TRF TO (.*)` etc.), applied `UCO.py:85-88`.
- **Kotak** – `BankRegexConstants.py:314-318` `CHQ_PATTERN1-4` (`MICR INWARD.*TO CLG (.*)`) plus `CHQ_CLEAN_KOTAK` (strips trailing bank names such as "AXIS BAN…", "STATE BAN…").
- Fund-transfer-by-cheque payees: `FT_CHQ_PATTERN1-37` `BankRegexConstants.py:263-299` (`^TRF FROM CHQ [0-9]+ (.*)`, `FUND TFR TO (.*)`, …) and `FT_PATTERN2/6` `:243,247`.
- **YES.py:116** `^CTS CLG DEL (.*)`.

### NEFT / RTGS credits
- **HDFC.py:157-161**: `^NEFT [CD][Rr]-<UTR>-…` → `sep_by_dash(3,4)` / `(2,4)` / `(2,3)`; `^NEFT\s?/` → `sep_by_(2,3)`; `^00…NEFT TO (.*)`; `:162` generic NEFT/RTGS/IMPS/IB → `sep_by_dash(2,3)`; `:226` blanks account-number-looking NEFT names.
- **SBI.py:116-122**: RTGS/NEFT INB forms (`SBI_INB_6-8`, `BankRegexConstants.py:48-50`); `:119` `NO:\s[A-Z0-9]+(.*)` capture; `:122` NEFT fallback `sep_by_star(3,4)` with digit/punct strip.
- **ICICI.py:152-158**: `^NEFT-|^RTGS-` → `sep_by_dash(2,3)`; `^INF/NEFT/|INF/INFT` → `sep_by_(3,4)`/`(4,5)`; `^RTGS/` → `sep_by_(3,4)`; NEFT/RTGS fallbacks; refinement at `:228-229`.
- **Union Bank** – `UB_NEFT_1-8_UNION`, `UB_RTGS_1-2_UNION` (`BankRegexConstants.py:120-129`, e.g. `^NEFT:IBUSER-(.*) SAA[0-9]+`, `RTGS:(.*) [A-Z]{4}[0-9]{12}`) applied `UnionBank.py:81-96`.
- **Kotak** – `NEFT_PATTERN0-7` `BankRegexConstants.py:206-213` (`^NEFT [0-9]+1DC (.*)`, `NEFT AXISCN[0-9]+ (.*)`…), `NEFT_CLEAN_KOTAK` `:214` (strips trailing IFSC-ish `IBKL.*| SBIN.*`), `KT_RTGS_PATTERN` `:217`.
- **YES.py:102-112**: `NEFT [CD][Rr] -`, `^NEFT O\s?/W [NP]…(.*)`, `^NEFT-[A-Z0-9]{11,13}-`, RTGS variants.
- **PNB** RTGS: `PNB_RTGS_KEYWORDS`/`PNB_RTGS_1` `BankRegexConstants.py:151-152`.

### UPI / IMPS person-to-person
- **HDFC.py:154,159,227-232,242,251**: `^UPI-` → `sep_by_dash(1,2)` (2nd token = payer/payee name); IMPS → `sep_by_dash(2,3)`; Razorpay/Paytm/UNREGISTERED special cases.
- **SBI.py:99** UPI → `sep_by_(3,4)` (4th `/`-token); IMPS via `SBI_IMPS_1-3` (`BankRegexConstants.py:60-62`) at `SBI.py:149-151`, junk suppression `:174-176,185`.
- **ICICI.py:139** UPI → `sep_by_(3,4)`; IMPS `:163-165` and refinements `:195-217,228-233` (Razorpay tokens, "…To X" splitting, IFSC-looking names re-extracted).
- **Kotak**: `IMPS_PATTERN1-8` `BankRegexConstants.py:195-202` (`^IMPS from (.*)Ref`, `IB IMPS TO (.*) Ref`…), `RCVD_FROM_IMPS1-5` `:234-238` (`^Received from (.*) IMPS REF` — the P2P credit form), `MB_TFR1` `:188`, `STOP_STRINGS` `:191`.
- **YES.py:96-99**: `^UPI/[0-9]+/From:(.*)/To` for credits, `/To:(.*)/` for debits.
- **UCO.py:65-77** and **UnionBank.py:98-105**, **TamilnadMerchantile.py:57-61** for their UPI/IMPS token positions.
- Global brand normalization: `UtilityScripts/CleanName.py` (`clean_names()`, 1,971 lines of partyName → canonical merchant mappings, e.g. `:1830` Google Pay, `:1745` `^EMI [0-9]+ CHQ` → "HDFC Bank Loan <num>"); cleanup constants `LOCATION_CLEAN`/`TRF_STOP_WORDS` `BankRegexConstants.py:64-65`, `HDFC_CLEAN1` `:106`, bank-name strippers `REMOVE_BANK_CB` `:417`, `REMOVE_BANK_CITI` `:424`, `CHQ_CLEAN_SCB` `:432`.
- Self/internal detection: `UtilityScripts/InternalPayment.py:8-62` (fuzzy match partyName vs account holder for categories listed at `:15`, incl. CHEQUE_PAID/CHEQUE_DEPOSIT/NEFT/IMPS/UPI).

## 4. Test fixtures / baseline corpus & test runner

**None exist in this repository.** Verified:
- Only 54 tracked files; no `tests/`, no `test_*.py`, no pytest/unittest imports, no `*.csv`/`*.json` fixtures anywhere under `/app` (and nothing in `/opt`, `/srv`, `/home`, `/root`).
- No pytest/tox/CI configuration; `setup.py` has no test deps.
- The only hints that test artifacts existed upstream are `.gitignore` entries `TEST*.xml` and `*.csv` — the baseline corpus (likely CSVs of transactions plus expected categories) was ignored/excluded from this import and is not present.
- Consequently there is no "diff against baseline" command available here. To test, you would have to POST a payload to `POST /categorizeTransaction` (fields: `bank`, `acc_type`, `accountUID`, `accountHolder`, `transactions` with `description`, `amount`, `type`, `balanceAfterTransaction`, `remark`) and diff the JSON yourself.

## 5. Git history

```
047782b import codebase   (only commit; branch: main; clean working tree; no stashes; no other branches)
```

The entire codebase was imported in a single squash commit (author `t <t@t>`, dated 2026-07-15), so per-file history for categorization/name-extraction logic is not recoverable from this repo — every file (HDFC.py, BankRegexConstants.py, CleanName.py, Purpose.py, etc.) was added in `047782b`.

### Quick reference: the files you'll touch for the three focus areas
| Concern | Primary files (path:lines) |
|---|---|
| Cheque debit categorization | `BankScripts/HDFC.py:69-75`, `BankScripts/SBI.py:44-47`, `BankScripts/ICICI.py:69-72`, `BankScripts/YES.py:45-46`, `BankScripts/UnionBank.py:50` |
| NEFT/RTGS/IMPS/UPI categorization | `BankScripts/HDFC.py:57-63`, `SBI.py:50-57`, `ICICI.py:61-68` (+ analogous block near top of every bank script) |
| Penny-drop / account verification | `UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py:6,69,75,110,116,133,163,321,327,365,396,410,415,428,431` + per-bank rule ~line 12 of each `BankScripts/*.py`; `UtilityScripts/Purpose.py:165,173` |
| Cheque payee name extraction | `BankRegexConstants.py:81-90,140-148,263-299,314-318,361-362,380-383`; `HDFC.py:163,188-197,260`; `SBI.py:123,135,164`; `UCO.py:85-88` |
| NEFT/UPI/IMPS name extraction | `BankRegexConstants.py:120-129,195-217,234-238`; `HDFC.py:146-246`; `SBI.py:97-192`; `ICICI.py:136-243`; `YES.py:96-116`; helpers `AppUtil.py:14-66`; normalization `CleanName.py` (whole file) |

"""Replay harness: run transactions through the same pipeline as Controller.py."""
import sys
import pandas as pd

import importlib

from categorizationapp.UtilityScripts import AppUtil
from categorizationapp.UtilityScripts.Purpose import purpose
from categorizationapp.UtilityScripts.CleanName import clean_names
from categorizationapp.UtilityScripts.InternalPayment import internal_payment

BANKS = {
    "HDFC": ("HDFC", "categorize_HDFC_transactions"),
    "SBI": ("SBI", "categorize_SBI_transactions"),
    "ICICI": ("ICICI", "categorize_ICICI_transactions"),
    "AXIS": ("Axis", "categorize_Axis_transactions"),
    "KOTAK": ("Kotak", "categorize_Kotak_transactions"),
    "YES": ("YES", "categorize_YES_transactions"),
    "RBL": ("RBL", "categorize_RBL_transactions"),
    "PNB": ("PNB", "categorize_PNB_transactions"),
    "UNION_BANK": ("UnionBank", "categorize_UnionBank_transactions"),
    "UCO": ("UCO", "categorize_UCO_transactions"),
    "IDFC": ("IDFC", "categorize_IDFC_transactions"),
    "IDBI": ("IDBI", "categorize_IDBI_transactions"),
    "BOB": ("BOB", "categorize_BOB_transactions"),
    "BOI": ("BOI", "categorize_BOI_transactions"),
    "CANARA": ("Canara", "categorize_Canara_transactions"),
    "FEDERAL": ("Federal", "categorize_Federal_transactions"),
    "INDUSIND": ("Indusind", "categorize_Indusind_transactions"),
    "CENTRAL_BANK": ("Central", "categorize_Central_transactions"),
    "KARUR_VYASA": ("KarurVyasa", "categorize_KarurVyasa_transactions"),
    "BANK_OF_MAHARASHTRA": ("BankOfMaharashtra", "categorize_BankOfMaharashtra_transactions"),
    "PAYTM_BANK": ("Paytm", "categorize_Paytm_transactions"),
    "STANDARD_CHARTERED": ("StandardCharted", "categorize_SCB_transactions"),
    "TAMILNAD": ("TamilnadMerchantile", "categorize_TamilnadMerchantile_transactions"),
    "SOUTH_INDIAN": ("SouthIndian", "categorize_SouthIndian_transactions"),
}


def run(bank, txns, acc_type="SAVING", holder="TEST HOLDER", full=True):
    mod_name, fn_name = BANKS[bank]
    mod = importlib.import_module(f"categorizationapp.BankScripts.{mod_name}")
    fn = getattr(mod, fn_name)
    df = pd.json_normalize(txns)
    for col in ("remark",):
        if col not in df.columns:
            df[col] = ""
    df = AppUtil.clean_input_df(df)
    if fn.__code__.co_argcount == 3 and "accountHolder" in fn.__code__.co_varnames[:3]:
        df = fn(df, acc_type, holder)
    else:
        try:
            df = fn(df, acc_type)
        except TypeError:
            df = fn(df, acc_type, holder)
    if full:
        df = purpose(df, acc_type)
        df = clean_names(df, acc_type, bank)
        if holder:
            df = internal_payment(df, holder, bank, acc_type)
    return df


def show(df):
    cols = [c for c in ["description", "remark", "type", "amount",
                        "transactionCategory", "transactionSubcategory", "partyName", "merchantType"]
            if c in df.columns]
    with pd.option_context("display.width", 250, "display.max_colwidth", 60):
        print(df[cols].to_string(index=False))


def T(description, type_="DEBIT", amount=5000, remark="", balance=100000):
    return {"description": description, "type": type_, "amount": amount,
            "remark": remark, "balanceAfterTransaction": balance}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # smoke test
    df = run("HDFC", [T("NEFT CR-SBIN0001234-JOHN DOE-JANE SMITH-N123456789012345", "CREDIT")])
    show(df)

todos.content: F-1: bare cheque-number debit note miscategorized as TRANSFER (PNB remark rule)
F-2: 'CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR' returns clearing tag instead of name (AU Small Finance)
F-3: NEFT credits with blank counterparty name (PNB py_extract index)
F-4: UPI P2P credit shows reference fragment instead of sender name (StanChart)
F-5: penny-drop verification credit filed as TRANSFER (Canara amount gate)
Verify fixes by replaying sample narrations through the pipeline

steps.message:
All five findings are resolved with one-line fixes across four bank scripts. Each was localized by replaying synthetic fixtures through the actual pipeline (bank script → `purpose` → `clean_names` → `internal_payment`) and pinpointing where the code contradicted either its own sibling rules or the QA-quoted narration.

## Root causes and fixes

**F-1 — bare cheque-number debit → TRANSFER** · `BankScripts/PNB.py:60`
The debit-side rule matched remarks of exactly 5 digits (`^[0-9]{5}$`) while its credit twin on line 61 accepts `^[0-9]{5,6}$`. Any 6-digit cheque number in the remark on a debit fell through every rule to the default TRANSFER. Restored to `^[0-9]{5,6}$`.

**F-2 — cleared cheque returns clearing tag as counterparty** · `BankScripts/AuSmallFinanceBank.py:78`
`^CHQ PAID-` used `sep_by_dash(1,2)`, which for `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR` returns dash-token 1 → "Micr Clg" (the internal clearing tag). The name sits at token 2. Restored to `sep_by_dash(2,3)` → "Ravi Kumar". The neighbouring `<NAME>-Chq Paid-…` layout (line 77) is untouched and still resolves.

**F-3 — NEFT credits with blank name** · `BankScripts/PNB.py:110`
The plain-`NEFT ` fallback used `py_extract(pat="NEFT (.*)", index=1)` — a one-capture-group pattern read at group index 1, which never exists, so `py_extract` always returned "". (Elsewhere in the codebase, `index=1` is only used with two-group patterns, e.g. `SBI_AUTOPAY7-9`.) Restored `index=0`. All the other PNB NEFT layouts (lines 97–109) were already correct and are unchanged.

**F-4 — instant-payment credit shows bare reference number** · `BankScripts/StandardCharted.py:113`
The `UPI-` dash-layout rule used `sep_by_dash(1,2)`, returning the 12-digit reference from `UPI-<ref>-<NAME>-…`. The sibling `IMPS-` rule in the same file (line 130) uses `(2,3)` for the identical `<scheme>-<ref>-<NAME>` shape. Restored to `sep_by_dash(2,3)`; the neighbouring `UPI/…` slash layouts (lines 114–117) still resolve as before.

**F-5 — penny-drop credit filed as TRANSFER** · `BankScripts/Canara.py:19`
The verification rule was gated on `amount.lt(1)`, which a ₹1 confirmation credit can never satisfy, so those rows fell to the transfer bucket. Every peer bank gates on `lt(2)` / `eq(1)` / `isin([1,-1])` (HDFC:13, PNB:12, RBL:15, etc.). Restored `amount.lt(2)`.

## Verification

- Each quoted/described form now derives the expected field (`CHEQUE_PAID`, "Ravi Kumar", non-blank NEFT name, "John Doe" instead of `512212345678`, `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`).
- Neighbouring layouts explicitly retested: 5-digit PNB remarks, credit-side cheque deposits, other PNB NEFT layouts, SCB slash-UPI and `IMPS-`, Canara non-penny credits and ordinary ₹1 deposits without verification keywords — all unchanged.
- All 35 bank scripts run through the full pipeline without errors.

Two inert oddities noticed but deliberately left alone (they cannot affect any output, and touching them risks moving baseline): a `<<<< INCONSISTENT >>>>` token inside a never-matching junk-filter regex at `BankScripts/RBL.py:137`, and a malformed dead rule (`&` where `,` belongs, evaluating to an always-False condition) at `BankScripts/UnionBank.py:100`.
